prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop website direction comp, first viewport only
Primary request: Create exactly one polished, shippable-looking homepage catalogue UI for fcullmann.com in the “Straight Utility Catalogue” direction: a familiar, conventional browser-tool catalogue executed with excellent restraint and craft. It should be instantly understandable as practical developer tools, not an experimental portfolio.
Reference interpretation: use the supplied category-standard light utility catalogue only as a craft bar for density, clarity, familiar card scanning, and an orderly six-column matrix. Do not copy its branding, logo, exact layout, navigation labels, iconography, tool content, or decorative background shapes.
Canvas: exactly 1504 × 1046 pixels, landscape, straight-on full-page capture. No browser chrome, no device frame.
Scene/backdrop: cool #F3F4F8 page background, clean and almost flat.
Composition/framing:
- Compact white header, about 64px tall, with a thin bottom border. At left an original simple coral-red rounded-square code-bracket mark followed by the wordmark “fcullmann.com”. At right, compact text navigation “Tools”, “Projects”, “Writing”, “About”, then a bordered language control “EN”.
- Centered hero below with generous but efficient spacing. Small coral eyebrow “TOOLS BY FLORIAN ULLMANN”. Exact heading “Developer tools for focused work”. Supporting copy in two short centered lines: “Fast, focused utilities that run in your browser — built and maintained by Florian, a Senior Software Engineer.”
- A centered row of compact category pills: “All”, “Format”, “Encode”, “Generate”, “Documents”. “All” is selected with coral-red fill and white text; others are white with subtle borders.
- Beneath, an orderly full-width six-column matrix of 12 tool cards in two rows, aligned to a centered max-width container. Cards are equal size, approximately 210px wide × 190px tall, with 18–20px gaps. Every card has a small friendly rounded-square functional icon tile at top, then title, concise two-line description, and a subtle arrow at lower right.
- First row card titles from left to right: “JSON Formatter”, “Base64 Encoder”, “UUID Generator”, “URL Encoder”, “PDF Converter”, “Color Converter”.
- Second row titles from left to right: “Unix Timestamp”, “Hash Generator”, “JWT Decoder”, “Markdown Preview”, “Regex Tester”, “Text Diff”.
- “JSON Formatter” is clearly Featured using a small coral pill reading “FEATURED” in its upper-right corner and a slightly stronger coral border, without making the card larger.
- “PDF Converter” is clearly unavailable using a small neutral pill reading “PLANNED”; keep the rest of that card softly muted.
- Use truthful concise descriptions only: JSON formatting and validation; Base64 text encode/decode; browser UUID generation; URL component encode/decode; PDF conversion planned; color value conversion; timestamp conversion; hashes; JWT inspection; markdown preview; regex testing; text comparison. No metrics or social proof.
- After the card grid, near the bottom fold, begin a white editorial section separated by a fine top border. Show the heading “Latest Writing” and the beginning of two restrained article rows, visibly continuing below the viewport. Use only neutral non-owner-specific placeholder article labels such as “Engineering notes” and “Practical browser APIs”, without dates or claims.
Style/medium: realistic high-fidelity production web UI mockup, precise modern CSS-like rendering, not concept art, not a wireframe. Strong modern sans-serif hierarchy similar to a tasteful neo-grotesk; crisp 1px borders; consistent 8px spacing rhythm; generous whitespace; restrained accessible contrast.
Color palette: #F3F4F8 background, pure white cards and header, #2A2D35 primary text, muted slate secondary text, coral-red #E74A3B primary accent. Functional icon tiles vary deliberately across coral, blue, green, violet, amber, and teal while remaining cohesive.
Materials/textures: rounded 14px cards, soft cool-gray borders, almost no shadow, no texture.
Text requirements: Render all quoted UI text exactly, correctly spelled, crisp, and legible. English UI only. Keep descriptions short enough to remain readable at this canvas size.
Product truth: Florian Ullmann is a Senior Software Engineer. The site presents browser developer tools, projects, and technical writing. Do not invent biography details, usage numbers, testimonials, clients, portrait, social links, project claims, or publishing dates.
Constraints: one desktop first viewport, exact six-column grid, polished practical spacing, visible Featured state, Latest Writing starts near the fold, original fcullmann.com visual identity.
Avoid: I Love PDF branding or logo, copied reference layout, PDF-centric tool content, Bootstrap styling, generic SaaS gradients, heavy shadows, glassmorphism, old atlas or paper styling, coordinates, serif typography, code-editor dark themes, illustrations, photography, portraits, browser chrome, device frame, watermarks, misspelled words, garbled text, extra navigation, fabricated facts.
